c:borrow_loaned_message.why: RFC-0010's zero-copy path. rcl/rclcpp borrow a TYPED message the middleware owns (`LoanedMessage<T>`, `borrow_loaned_message`, `publish_loaned_message`, `return_loaned_message_from_publisher`); ours is a TOKEN over a byte range (`loan`/`commit`/`discard` on the publisher, `borrow`/`release` on the subscription) because C has no templates and the wrapper would need an allocator to own. NOTE the verbs differ as well as the shape, and only the shape has a reason -- W5 should decide whether `loan`/`commit`/`discard` should read `borrow_loaned_message`/`publish_loaned_message`/`return_loaned_message`.

c:event_publisher_count_cb_t.why: QoS events. rclcpp routes every event through one `set_on_new_qos_event_callback` plus a `QOSEventHandler` waitable the executor polls; ours are named callbacks per event (`on_liveliness_lost`, `on_offered_deadline_missed`, `on_message_lost`) registered on the entity. Constraint: no allocator for a per-event handler object and no wait-set to poll it from -- the callback is a fn-ptr in the entity's own static storage. The set of events is the same. This one reports matched-subscription count changes, which rclcpp answers by POLLING `get_subscription_count` -- see that row.

c:executor_add_subscription_in_group.why: adds a subscription to a named callback group, which rclc has no concept of (rclcpp does -- see `cpp:Node::create_callback_group` in the exec stage). Needed because RFC-0002 maps groups onto RTOS priority tiers.

c:executor_add_subscription_raw_with_inf.why: the raw + message-info form; see `c:publish_raw` and `rust:RawMessageInfo`.

c:executor_get_publishers_info_by_topic.why: phase-381 W3/W4. Same verb as ROS 2; the RECEIVER differs. ROS 2 hangs the graph off a node because each Node/Context owns a participant; a nano-ros image opens ONE session for the whole image -- a session per node is RAM a 128 KiB target does not have -- and the Executor owns it. NOT a `rename`: the name follows the receiver, and the receiver is where the session is. The endpoint carries no QoS. The GRANTED profile is what answers 'why is nothing arriving', no backend can read one back yet, and reporting the remote's DECLARED profile would be a confident wrong answer -- so the field is absent here and the rmw ABI's `*_UNKNOWN` sentinels carry it at the vtable seam, which is that ABI's documented way to say 'could not determine'.

c:get_zero_initialized_publisher.why: rcl's free-function spelling; ours is `nros_publisher_get_zero_initialized`, a method-style name on the type. See `c:get_zero_initialized_node`.

c:get_zero_initialized_subscription_cont.why: content-filtered topics are a DDS feature: the subscriber ships an SQL-ish expression the WRITER evaluates. Only one of our backends is DDS, and the filter would have to be a no-op on zenoh and XRCE -- a QoS-shaped promise two of three transports cannot keep. Same reasoning `rmw-api-parity.py` already records for `rmw_*_content_filter`.

c:message_type_t.why: the typesupport handle a publisher or subscription is created with. rosidl's `rosidl_message_type_support_t` carries function pointers into generated code plus an identifier used to pick a middleware-specific implementation at RUNTIME; ours names the one linked backend's descriptor, because an image has exactly one.

c:publish.why:
CORRECTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5), re-verdicted rename -> divergence. The previous text argued from `nros_publisher_publish`, a symbol that has never existed: the only occurrence of that spelling anywhere in the tree is a comment in `examples/native/c/custom-transport-loopback/src/main.c` recording that phase 212 replaced the never-defined name. Our C publish entry points are `nros_publish_raw(publisher, data, len)` for the byte form and the codegen'd per-message `<pkg>_<msg>_publish(publisher, msg)` for the typed form (`packs/c/message.h.jinja`, e.g. `std_msgs_msg_int32_publish`). BOTH already have rcl's shape -- a free function taking the publisher first -- so there is no free-function-vs-method rename here. The cited precedent does not apply either, twice over: `c:get_zero_initialized_publisher` is verdict DECLINED, i.e. it argues for KEEPING our spelling, and it declines because ours there IS method-style, which ours here is not.
What actually differs is the SHAPE, and a platform constraint is why. `rcl_publish(publisher, ros_message, allocation)` is ONE type-erased function over a `const void *` ROS message plus an `rmw_publisher_allocation_t *`. We have no runtime typesupport dispatch and no allocator, so the typed publish is generated per message type (concrete struct pointer, no typesupport lookup, serializes into a `NROS_PUB_BUFFER_SIZE` stack buffer) and the type-erased publish is byte-oriented. The generated typed helper lives in a message header, which the report drops as message plumbing -- that, not an absence, is why this row reads theirs-only.
The `_raw` suffix on the byte form is a separate and still-open question, tracked by the SERIALIZED -> RAW pair (`c:take_serialized_message`, `c:publish_serialized_message`). It is not this row's.

rename.resolution: Not a rename. The word and the free-function shape already match; the row's premise (nros_publisher_publish) was a symbol that does not exist. Re-verdicted to divergence, naming the two real differences and their constraints: no `rmw_publisher_allocation_t` (no allocator) and per-type codegen instead of a `const void *` (no runtime typesupport dispatch). No code change; no target name invented.

rename.resolution:
Target settled 2026-09-03 alongside the RECEIVE half, which did land: `nros_subscription_take_serialized` (`nros_generated.h:6459`) with `try_recv_raw` surviving as a `NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG` forwarder. This is the transmit half, unexecuted.

Scope is wider than this C row implies: three ours-only halves are already rowed (`c:publish_raw`, `cpp:Publisher::publish_raw`, `rust:Publisher::publish_raw`), plus the `nros_cpp_publish_raw` FFI symbol and the C message template, which emits `return nros_publish_raw(...)` in generated code. Confirm the exact target symbol before executing — the row names the word `serialized` but never the symbol.

c:publisher_get_actual_qos.why:
reports the QoS an entity actually ended up with, which can differ from what its call site requested. RE-VERDICTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417), declined -> gap, and the old justification DELETED rather than patched. It said QoS is selected at COMPILE time, so actual and requested are the same value by construction and an accessor would return its own input. That is false in both languages. QoS is a RUNTIME argument here (`nros_publisher_init_with_options(..., const struct nros_qos_t *qos, ...)`; `Node::create_publisher<M>(out, topic, qos)`), and a launch-lowered override table changes it AFTER the call site: `nros_node_set_qos_overrides` (`nros_generated.h:5205`) and `Node::set_qos_overrides` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/node.hpp:292`) install `nros_qos_override_t` / `nros_cpp_qos_override_t` rows, and every entity created afterwards folds the matching `(topic, role)` entries in before the backend-compat check (`apply_qos_overrides`, `packages/api/nros-cpp/src/lib.rs:1283`, `packages/api/nros-c/src/qos.rs:194`). Actual differs from requested exactly when a deploy plan says so -- which is the accessor's whole use case. Nobody has built the readback: the folded profile is handed to the backend and not retained for a getter. That is a gap, not a decline.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-14, CORRECTED — the finding as recorded said six `*_get_actual_qos` implementations "echo the request", and that headline is FALSE for this checkout. `read_entity_qos` (`packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/qos.cpp:140`) does a REAL read-back: `dds_get_qos` then `dds_qget_{reliability,durability,history,deadline,lifespan,liveliness}` (issue 0823 / phase-393 W1), and all six thunks call it.

THE DEFENSIBLE STATEMENT IS NARROWER AND STILL A DIVERGENCE. `out` arrives PRE-LOADED with the request — the caller does `let mut granted = qos_struct;` before invoking the slot (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/lib.rs`) — and `read_entity_qos` overwrites only the fields whose `dds_qget_*` returns true. So every field Cyclone CANNOT report reads back as the REQUESTED value. Upstream's `rmw.h` requires `*_UNKNOWN` for exactly that case, and the one consumer compares requested against granted — so an unreportable field reads as GRANTED, the inverse of upstream's meaning. The code says so itself at `qos.cpp:134` and the header repeats it at `packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_entity.h` (that header sentence is now itself imprecise, since the REPORTABLE fields no longer echo).

THE `*_UNKNOWN` SUB-CLAIM IS CONFIRMED BY GREP: the only non-test writes of any `*_UNKNOWN` value in the tree are in the graph endpoint-info trampoline (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/rust_adapter.rs`), NOT a `get_actual_qos`. No `*_get_actual_qos` implementation anywhere writes one — the slots whose own documentation defines the contract are exactly the ones that do not honour it. Every backend other than Cyclone leaves the six slots NULL.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: this row's `gap` verdict already says the READBACK is not exposed to a C or C++ caller, so today nobody can observe it — a Rust user cannot reach it at all (`grep -rn actual_qos` over the facade and the node handles finds nothing; the read-back is consumed only by `report_qos_downgrade`). That is what makes this the moment to record it: closing the gap by surfacing the accessor would ship the inverted meaning to users, so the disposition ADOPT covers BOTH halves — expose the accessor AND write `*_UNKNOWN` for a policy the backend cannot report. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

c:publisher_get_context.why: reaches the context a publisher was created on. There is no separate context object -- see the init stage's `c:context_*`.

c:publisher_get_options.why: reads back the options a publisher was created with. `nros_publisher_options_t` ships (`nros_generated.h:2467-2474`) and `nros_publisher_init_with_options` takes it; what is missing is the READBACK -- nothing retains the struct on the handle and no `*_get_options` exists anywhere in our C surface, for any entity. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): this row said there is no runtime options struct. Seven ship and the correlator buckets all fourteen items `same` -- `nros_{node,publisher,subscription,service,client,action_client,action_server}_options_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:1461,1729,2011,2474,2537,2556,2592`) plus a `*_get_default_options` for each, and `nros_node_options_t::domain_id_override` is a RUNTIME per-node domain. What is genuinely absent is the LIFECYCLE around one: no `*_options_copy`, no `*_options_fini`, and no `*_get_options` readback anywhere in the C surface.

c:publisher_get_subscription_count.why: how many subscriptions are matched, RIGHT NOW. We notify on change (`nros_event_publisher_count_cb_t` + `nros_count_status_t`) and never let a caller ask, so code that wants to skip work when nobody is listening has to keep its own mirror of the callback's last value. Both forms are useful and rclcpp ships both. Phase 379 W3.

c:publisher_init_default.why:
rclc's convenience wrapper: publisher with the default QoS. `nros_publisher_init` takes no QoS and IS the default form; `nros_publisher_init_with_qos` is the explicit one.

see `cpp:Publisher::Publisher<M>`.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-27, recorded on this key because the extractor does not emit destructors: the MOVE CONSTRUCTOR and move-assignment carry the same defect and do surface here.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: an `rclcpp` subscription is owned by a `shared_ptr` the node holds, so destroying or relocating the user's handle cannot leave the executor dispatching into it.

OURS: the destructor (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/subscription.hpp:451`) unregisters only in POLL mode — `if (initialized_ && !callback_mode_)`. In callback mode it clears a flag and nothing else, and NO unregister FFI exists at all (`grep -n "unregister\|deregister" packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/nros_cpp_ffi.h` finds nothing). The arena still holds `&out` as its dispatch context. The move constructor (`:465`) and move-assignment (`:480`) are the same shape: they copy the callback fields, SKIP the relocate for callback mode, and clear `other.initialized_` — leaving the arena pointing at the moved-from object.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: RUNTIME UB, unattributable. The next `spin_once` calls the trampoline with a pointer to a destroyed or moved-from object, at an arbitrary later tick, with nothing naming the subscription. THE ONLY GUARD IS PROSE — the class comment at `:461` and a `@param`-level "CONSTRAINT: do not move `out` after this returns" at `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/node.hpp:581`. No `= delete`, no `static_assert`, no runtime check. RFC-0089 says a refusal fires at the earliest point the defect is KNOWABLE, and for a move that point is the TYPE: deleting the move operations in callback mode makes it a compile error. (The `rclcpp::Node` adapter path is safe by construction — `owned_entities_` pins the cell for the node's lifetime.) Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

DISPOSITION REFUSE-LOUD, recorded in the field. For a move the defect is knowable from the TYPE, which RFC-0089 makes the earliest point loudness is available: `= delete` the move constructor and move-assignment in callback mode, so relocating a dispatching subscription is a compile error naming the constraint, instead of a comment asking the user not to.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt-bounded, because a refusal that is only OWED is not a refusal. The paragraph above records the decision (delete the move operations in callback mode); nothing in the header does it yet, and a row reads as the shipped state.

WHAT THE COMPILER POINTS AT: the constructor set. Ours is the default constructor (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/subscription.hpp:505`), a move constructor and move-assignment (`:465`, `:480`), and deleted copies (`:549`). Upstream's `Subscription(node_base, type_support, topic, qos, callback, options, ...)` is not among them, so naming it is `no matching constructor` — and a ported file rarely does: rclcpp constructs subscriptions through `Node::create_subscription`, which is `cpp:Node::create_subscription`'s row.

THE ENVELOPE, and the half that is NOT loud: a callback-mode subscription must not be moved after registration (the arena holds `this` as the trampoline context) and the only guard is prose (`:461`, and `node.hpp`'s CONSTRAINT note). RFC-0089 puts that refusal at the TYPE; until the `= delete` lands this row is adopt-bounded with the envelope stated here and in the header, and the deletion stays owed.

see `cpp:MessageInfo`.

phase-428 W6 (2026-09-06) — disposition, required because this row's SHAPE CORRESPONDS: the name exists on the ported surface and the correlator files it `same`, so nothing in a build says the contract differs. That is the class RFC-0089 exists for.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclrs::MessageInfo` wraps `rmw_message_info_t` and exposes it whole.

OURS: `packages/core/nros-core/src/message_info.rs:24` — a flat struct of source/received timestamps, publication/reception sequence numbers and a 16-byte `publisher_gid`. See `cpp:MessageInfo` for why the DDS-shaped whole is not carried.
